options: A small, simple chart with no legend, axis lines, or labels, usually nested in a table or matrix cell
A full chart with an extra-large legend
A type of dataset parameter
A gauge with a needle pointer
questions.explain: A sparkline strips away the supporting chart elements — legend, axis lines, labels, tick marks — to convey a lot of information in very little space, typically right inside a table cell.

questions.q: Why can't you add a sparkline to a detail row of a table?
options: Sparklines display aggregated data, so they must go in a cell associated with a group
Detail rows don't support any charts at all
Sparklines require at least three datasets
Detail rows can only contain text fields
questions.explain: Because sparklines display aggregated data, they have to go in a cell associated with a group — a group total row, not a per-record detail row.

questions.q: What's the main difference between a sparkline and a data bar?
options: A sparkline typically plots multiple points as a line; a data bar typically represents data as a bar
Data bars can never represent more than one value
Sparklines can only be pie charts
There is no difference — they are the same feature under different names
questions.explain: Sparklines almost always plot multiple data points over time as a line, while data bars represent the data as a bar — though a data bar can still be stacked to show more than one value.

questions.q: Why does "alignment" matter when several sparklines sit in the same table column?
options: Without matching horizontal and vertical scales, rows aren't actually comparable to each other
Alignment only affects the color of the sparkline
It determines which dataset the sparkline uses
Misaligned sparklines will fail to render
questions.explain: If sparklines in the same column don't share horizontal alignment (same time period lines up) and vertical alignment (same value reaches the same height), a row with only small values would stretch to fill the cell, making it look misleadingly dramatic next to a row with an actual spike.

questions.q: How do you turn a sparkline back into a full chart with axes and a legend?
options: Right-click the sparkline and select Convert to Full Chart
Delete the sparkline and manually rebuild every element
It's not possible — full charts and sparklines are unrelated features
Change the dataset's data type
questions.explain: Because a sparkline is just a chart with extra elements hidden, right-clicking it and choosing Convert to Full Chart restores the axis lines, labels, tick marks, and legend instantly.
